info.name: Egoola API — Accounts & Auth
info.description:
Covers what's built so far: Admin/Seller/Buyer login (JWT) + token refresh, and Admin-only Admin/Seller/Buyer management.

How to use:
1. Pick the `Egoola - Local` environment (or edit `base_url`).
2. Run any request in **Auth** first — its "Tests" script saves the returned `access`/`refresh` tokens into collection variables automatically.
3. Every request under **Accounts** already sends `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` — no manual copy-pasting needed.
4. When a 401 says the token expired, run **Auth > Refresh Token** — it re-saves `access_token` the same way.

All accounts endpoints require an Admin token (401 = no/invalid token, 403 = valid token but wrong role — see docs/authentication.md in the repo).

For Country/State/City/Thana reference-data management, see the separate Egoola API — Geography collection. For the full Seller Verification workflow (verify/reject with a mandatory note, verification_logs history) and deeper Seller-only coverage (business info, media upload), see the separate Egoola API — Seller collection.

request.description: Public endpoint — no token needed to call this. Returns access + refresh JWTs carrying actor_type=admin.

Public endpoint. Logs in an Admin whose type is super_admin. Admin Management (the **Admins** folder) is super-admin only — a plain admin token from "Admin Login" gets 403 there. Saves the token as `super_admin_token`, which the Admins folder uses.

Public endpoint. A seller logs in with **phone number + password** (admins and buyers use email). Returns a token carrying actor_type=seller — will get 403 on every Accounts endpoint below (those are Admin-only), which is expected until Seller self-service routes exist.

exec: console.log('Saved seller access token as seller_token (not used by Accounts requests below — those need an admin token).');

request.description: Public endpoint. Returns a token carrying actor_type=user (buyer).

exec: console.log('Saved buyer access token as buyer_token (not used by Accounts requests below — those need an admin token).');

request.description: Exchanges the saved refresh token (14-day life) for a new access token (1-hour life) — the actor_type/actor_id claims carry over automatically. Run this instead of logging in again once the access token expires.

item.name: Admins

request.description: Admin-only. Returns the list-view fields (no media, no full geography — see AdminListSerializer).
`password` is required on create (hashed server-side), optional on update. `type` choices: super_admin, admin (super-admin only endpoint).
Full detail view — includes media[] and geography fields, unlike the list view.
PUT replaces the whole record — `password` can be left out on update (only re-hashed if you send a new one).
Preferred for small edits — only send the field(s) you're changing.

item.description: Super-admin only. Run **Auth > Super-Admin Login** first. A plain admin, seller or buyer token gets 403. Types are `super_admin` and `admin`. You can't change your own type/status or delete yourself (400).

request.description: `info` is the seller's business profile (1:1) — created/updated in the same call. `verification_status`/`verification_note` are now writable (see the dedicated Egoola API — Seller collection for the full verification workflow, including the mandatory rejection note and the verification_logs history); wallet/bonus fields stay read-only from the client, managed by the (future) wallet flow instead.

Admin-only. Light rows (no media). Filters: search, status, country, state, city, thana, email_verified, phone_verified, created_from, created_to — combine freely. Paginated with limit/offset. Full detail (media, address, skills) is on Retrieve Buyer. See docs/buyer-management-guide.md.
Note: the model/table is called `User` in code (see apps/accounts/models.py docstring) — this is the Buyer, not Django's own auth user.

item.name: Carts & Wishlists (admin)
item.description: Admin, read-only oversight of buyers' carts and wishlists — no create/update/delete here, buyers manage their own through the buyer-facing API (see Egoola-BuyerApp). Needs an Admin token (super-admin or plain admin, both work). See docs/cart-wishlist-admin-guide.md.

item.name: Carts
item.description: Read-only (list + detail): every buyer's cart. A cart never spans sellers — every row belongs to exactly one seller, or to none (admin-owned listings). See docs/cart-wishlist-admin-guide.md section 1.

exec: const results = pm.response.json().results; if (results && results.length) { pm.collectionVariables.set('cart_id', results[0].id); }

query.description: matches the buyer's name, email or phone
exact seller id; use 0 for the shared no-seller cart
only carts holding this listing id

item.name: Favourites
item.description: Read-only (list + detail): every buyer's saved listing, regardless of whether it is still publicly visible — see `listing_visible`. See docs/cart-wishlist-admin-guide.md section 2.

exec: const results = pm.response.json().results; if (results && results.length) { pm.collectionVariables.set('favourite_id', results[0].id); }

query.description: matches the buyer's name/email/phone or the listing's title
true | false — currently passes the buyer-facing visibility rule

item.name: Bidding
Create a bid on the seller's behalf

request.description: "Admin can do everything": place a bid for any seller. `listing` (the job) and `bidder` (the seller) are both required.

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('bid_bid1_id', b.id); pm.collectionVariables.set('bid_tier1_id', b.price_tiers[0].id);
pm.test('Status is 200, only this seller\'s bid', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().results.length).to.eql(1); });

pm.test('Status is 200, job and bidder briefs', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.job).to.have.property('buyer'); pm.expect(b.bidder).to.have.property('phone'); });

item.name: Edit a pending bid — price-tier reconcile

exec: pm.test('Status is 200, now two tiers', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().price_tiers.length).to.eql(2); });

request.description: Same effect as the buyer's own `/buyer/jobs/{id}/bids/{id}/accept/`: an Order is created directly, and the job moves to `in_progress`.

item.name: Confirm the rival bid was auto-rejected
Reject the accepted bid — no reason (expect 400)
Reject the accepted bid — undo the hire

request.description: Undoes an already-accepted hire **without** cancelling the job itself (that's the separate admin-only job move — see the **Jobs** folder in `Egoola-Listing.postman_collection.json`). This bid -> `rejected` (it *was* judged, the other way); the job reopens; the Order behind it is cancelled.

item.name: Confirm the job reopened to open_for_bidding
Confirm the earlier auto-rejected bid is untouched

request.description: The sellers may place a fresh bid if they want back in; nothing about an earlier loss is restored by someone else's hire falling through.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200, still rejected (not restored)', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().status).to.eql('rejected'); });

item.description: Admin oversight of every bid, plus "do everything": create a bid on any seller's behalf, accept one on the buyer's behalf, or undo an already-accepted hire. A job itself (create on a buyer's behalf, the admin-only `in_progress -> cancelled` move) is the **Jobs** folder in `Egoola-Listing.postman_collection.json`. Full reference: `docs/job-bidding-guide.md`. Order oversight (a job's hire creates one directly, no cart) isn't browsable via API yet — the next step.
